preamble: Middle Chinese voiced stops [b] became voiceless in Mandarin; in the level tone (平聲) they surfaced aspirated [pʰ], while in the oblique tones they merged with plain [p] (see b_to_p). The split is conditioned by the original tone category.
sources: Pulleyblank, E. G. (1984). Middle Chinese: A Study in Historical Phonology. University of British Columbia Press.
Norman, J. (1988). Chinese. Cambridge University Press.
